subject: Renewal: phased SLO uplift + burst credits proposal
messages:
From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@heliospay.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliospay.com
Date: 2028-06-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — latency tail & support path

Hi Vivek,

Hope you had a good week. Our annual renewal is coming up in late July and we need to lock in both term and support levels. Over the last 6 months we've migrated key payment flows to Redwood and have been happy with throughput, but we've seen several p99 latency spikes during peak settlement windows that impact reconciliation jobs.

Procurement asked me to start a conversation around upgrading to a premium SLA at renewal with clearer p99 latency SLOs and an option for burst capacity credits for Black Friday-style days.

Can your team propose an approach that:
- Lets us preserve current commit pricing for year 1
- Shows a phased SLO ramp (baseline -> premium) so we can justify budget
- Includes an ops/oncall handoff and faster response SLAs for production incidents

I've attached our Q2 usage export and the internal runbook notes. Procurement (cc'ed) will want a timeline to review redlines.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Grant
Head of Platform Reliability
HeliosPay

Attachments: HeliosPay_usage_report_Q2.csv
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@heliospay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — latency tail & support path

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the context and the export. Glad to hear the migration is going well overall.

Quick proposal: we can offer a staged SLA uplift tied to a capacity reservation ladder. High level:
- Phase 1 (start of contract): Dedicated reserved capacity sized to current 95th percentile throughput; SLO: p99 <= 350ms, response RTO 1 hour for Sev1 incidents.
- Phase 2 (after 90 days): Option to enable premium tier for p99 <= 200ms with a soft launch period and a performance credit if we miss the target more than twice in a 30-day window.
- Burst credits: one pool of 72 hours per quarter that HeliosPay can draw from for traffic spikes; additional hours billed at a pre-agreed incremental rate.

I'll pull in Lauren and Marcus to draft a formal one-pager and a pricing worksheet that keeps your year-1 commit intact and shows the marginal cost of the phase-2 uplift. Can you confirm the org's preferred signatory and procurement timeline?

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@heliospay.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — latency tail & support path

Alyssa — looping in our renewals playbook and a concrete SLO ladder suggestion. Attached: SLA_Proposal_v3.pdf and burst-credit-examples.docx.

Proposal details (short):
- Baseline (Committed): p95 <= 120ms; p99 <= 350ms; 99.5% availability window; Standard Support (business hours)
- Premium (add-on after 90d): p95 <= 70ms; p99 <= 200ms; 99.9% availability; 24/7 Priority Support + 30 min initial response for Sev1 incidents
- Performance Credit: credits applied to invoice if p99 exceeds target for >2 days in 30-day window (tiered: 10% / 25% / 50% depending on severity)
- Burst Credits: one-time quarterly pool (default 72 hours). If pool exhausted, short-term burst capacity available at $X/hr (see spreadsheet).

We kept the year-1 committed spend unchanged in the model and showed the delta to enable premium in Q4. Marcus — can you confirm GPU sizing assumptions used in the pricing sheet?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Proposal_v3.pdf; burst-credit-examples.docx
From: Evan Marks <evan@heliospay.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@heliospay.com>, procurement@heliospay.com
Date: 2028-06-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — latency tail & support path

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple of constraints from our side:
- Procurement needs the contract redline window to be no longer than 10 business days.
- Finance prefers to avoid a full upgrade at renewal; they'd accept a 2-step ramp if the first 6 months are at current commit with the dedicated reservation and the premium SLO flagged as an optional add-on to enable after a 90-day validation.
- For burst credits, we'd like a monthly reporting cadence that shows usage and remaining pool.

If you can provide a DocuSign-ready amendment and a short mutual action plan (owner / due dates), we can route internally. Also please mark the person who will sign the SOW on Redwood's side.

Evan Marks
Head of Procurement
HeliosPay
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Evan Marks <evan@heliospay.com>, Alyssa Grant <alyssa@heliospay.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — latency tail & support path

Evan / Alyssa — thanks. Summary and next steps below; I'll own the SOW signature on Redwood's side unless legal flags anything.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- Tue 2028-07-03: Redwood sends DocuSign amendment (term + baseline dedicated reservation + premium SLO addendum + burst credits appendix). Owner: Vivek.
- Fri 2028-07-07: HeliosPay initial redline due. Owner: Evan/Alyssa.
- Mon 2028-07-10: Finalize pricing and attach redline; Redwood provides final dedicated sizing worksheet. Owner: Marcus.
- Mon 2028-07-17: Expected sign (if redlines complete).

Pricing note: we've preserved your year-1 committed spend in the worksheet and attached an optional premium uplift that is billed only if you enable Phase 2. See attached spreadsheet: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx.

Reporting: we'll provide a monthly burst-credit dashboard and a weekly SLO digest during the 90-day validation window.

Please confirm the signatory name we should populate in the signature block (HeliosPay side). Once you confirm, I'll trigger the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
